items.author: ian-reay
items.body:
Aider is a coding assistant ( https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider ). It helps people write better code. But its built on a strategy where it takes universal c-tags and loads the tags ( your code's structure ) into the context window. As a result, it can only handle small applications. Applications with a few thousand lines of code ( which is many ) just cannot be handled by packing the system prompt with this much information. 

I think there is huge opportunity for a solution like MemGPT to realistically help and nurture coding assistants to effectively work on large code bases.
items.title: Integration with Aider

items.author: cpacker
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Grammar is hardcoded to the base functions - if you use the new [custom functions](https://memgpt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/functions/), you cannot use [grammar-based sampling](https://github.com/cpacker/MemGPT/blob/main/memgpt/local_llm/grammars/json_func_calls_with_inner_thoughts.gbnf) since the grammar will only allow sampling based on prior functions.

To fix we need to dynamically generate the grammar file based on the linked functions.
items.title: Grammar does not update with new functions
